title: Querying Data: Server vs Client
description: Fetch data using Prisma Client inside Server Components, getServerSideProps, and understand when to use each.

slides.title: The Right Place to Query 🎯
slides.content:
# Server‑Side Data Fetching

Prisma Client should **never** be imported into client components or sent to the browser. It can only run in:

* `getServerSideProps` / `getStaticProps` (Pages Router)
* Server Components (App Router)
* API Routes
* Server Actions

This keeps your database credentials secure and leverages server‑side rendering.

slides.content: Query all posts and pass them as props.

quizData.question: Why can't Prisma Client be used directly in a client component?

options.text: It's too slow for the browser
It would expose database connection details and the query engine only works in Node.js
It's against Next.js rules but technically possible

quizData.explanation: Prisma Client contains database credentials and uses Node.js APIs that don't exist in the browser, making it a server‑only module.

App Router Example (app/page.js)
slides.content: The simplest possible page with database data.

quizData.question: In an App Router Server Component, where does the database query run?

options.text: In the browser after JavaScript loads
On the server at request time (or build time for static)

quizData.explanation: Server Components execute exclusively on the server, so Prisma queries happen there and never reach the client.

slides.title: API Routes for Client‑Side Queries 🌉
Deciding Strategy ✨
slides.content: Use Server Components (or getServerSideProps) for initial page data. Use API routes for client‑side mutations or data that changes based on client state. This keeps your app fast and secure.
